abstract_html: A branched triple cover of a genus-two curve can change the local curve count while preserving all determinant signs on unramified covers of degrees at most seven. At the crossing the degree-three elementary multiplicity in genus five changes by two in absolute value. At a generic transverse crossing on a prescribed simply branched triple cover with symmetric monodromy over a curve of genus at least two, we determine the local Gromov–Witten change in degree seven and every source genus. Each nonempty subset of branch values gives a nodal map joining the sextic Galois closure to the original curve. Its contribution is the degree-one series of a smooth curve, with sign determined by the number of nodes and the sum of their branch weights, up to a common orientation sign. On a fixed symplectic six-torus the other curves compensate each change in the same integral homology class and elementary genus.
